readings.title: Solomon's Officials and Governors
readings.subtitle: The twelve governors who provided for the royal household.
readings.text: [1 Kings 4:1] And it came to be that Sovereign Shelomoh was sovereign over all Yisra’ěl. [2] And these were his chief officials: Azaryahu son of Tsaḏoq, the priest; [3] Eliḥoreph and Aḥiyah, sons of Shisha, scribes; Yehoshaphat son of Aḥiluḏ, the recorder; [4] and Benayahu son of Yehoyaḏa, over the army; and Tsaḏoq and Eḇyathar, the priests; [5] and Azaryahu son of Nathan, over the officers; Zaḇuḏ son of Nathan, a priest, friend of the sovereign; [6] and Aḥishar, over the household; and Aḏoniram son of Aḇda, over the compulsory labour. [7] And Shelomoh had twelve governors over all Yisra’ěl, who provided food for the sovereign and his household – each one made provision for one new moon of the year – [8] and these were their names: Ben-Ḥur, in the mountains of Ephrayim; [9] Ben-Deqer, in Maqats and Sha‛alḇim and Běyth Shemesh and Ělon Běyth Ḥanan; [10] Ben-Ḥeseḏ in Arubboth, Soḵoh and all the land of Ḥěpher were his; [11] Ben-Aḇinaḏaḇ, all the height of Dor, Taphath the daughter of Shelomoh became his wife; [12] Ba‛ana son of Aḥiluḏ, in Ta‛anaḵ and Meḡiddo, and all Běyth She’an, which is beside Tsarethan below Yizre‛ěl, from Běyth She’an to Aḇěl Meḥolah, as far as the other side of Yoqne‛am; [13] Ben-Geḇer, in Ramoth Gil‛aḏ, the towns of Ya’ir son of Menashsheh in Gil‛aḏ were his; the portion of Argoḇ in Bashan, sixty large cities with walls and bronze gate-bars, were his; [14] Aḥinaḏaḇ son of Iddo, in Maḥanayim; [15] Aḥima‛ats in Naphtali; he also took <dn>את</dn> Basemath the daughter of Shelomoh as wife; [16] Ba‛anah son of Ḥushai, in Ashěr and in Aloth; [17] Yehoshaphat son of Paruvaḥ, in Yissasḵar; [18] Shim‛i son of Ělah, in Binyamin; [19] Geḇer son of Uri, in the land of Gil‛aḏ, in the land of Siḥon sovereign of the Amorites and of Oḡ sovereign of Bashan, and one governor was in the land.

readings.title: The Extent and Peace of Solomon's Kingdom
readings.subtitle: His provisions, his wisdom, and his international fame.
readings.text: [1 Kings 4:20] Yehuḏah and Yisra’ěl were as numerous as the sand by the sea, eating and drinking and rejoicing. [21] And Shelomoh was ruling over all reigns from the River to the land of the Philistines, as far as the border of Mitsrayim. They did taskwork and served <dn>את</dn> Shelomoh all the days of his life. [22] And Shelomoh’s food supply for one day was thirty kors of fine flour, and sixty kors of meal, [23] ten fatted cattle and twenty cattle from the pastures, and one hundred sheep, besides deer, and gazelles, and roebucks, and fatted fowl. [24] For he was ruling over all on this side of the River from Tiphsaḥ even to Azzah, over all the sovereigns on this side of the River. And he had peace on all sides round about him. [25] And Yehuḏah and Yisra’ěl dwelt safely, each man under his vine and his fig tree, from Dan as far as Be’ěrsheḇa, all the days of Shelomoh. [26] And Shelomoh had forty thousand stalls of horses for his chariots, and twelve thousand horsemen. [27] And these governors, each one in his new moon, provided food for Sovereign Shelomoh and for all who came to the table of Sovereign Shelomoh. There was no lack in their supply. [28] They also brought <dn>את</dn> barley and <dn>את</dn> straw to the appointed place, for the horses and steeds, each one according to his right-ruling. [29] And <dn>Elohim</dn> gave Shelomoh exceeding great wisdom and understanding, and largeness of heart like the sand on the seashore. [30] And Shelomoh’s wisdom excelled the wisdom of all the men of the East and all the wisdom of Mitsrayim. [31] For he was wiser than all men, than Ěythan the Ezrahite, and Hěman, and Kalkol, and Darda, the sons of Maḥol. And his name was in all the nations round about. [32] And he spoke three thousand proverbs, and his songs were one thousand and five. [33] And he spoke of trees, from the cedar tree of Leḇanon even to the hyssop that springs out of the wall. And he spoke of beasts, and of birds, and of creeping creatures, and of fish. [34] And there came from all peoples, from all the sovereigns of the earth who had heard of his wisdom, to hear <dn>את</dn> the wisdom of Shelomoh.

readings.title: A Prayer for the King's Righteous Reign
readings.subtitle: May his dominion be everlasting and his name endure forever.
readings.text: [Psalm 72:1] O <dn>Elohim</dn>, give <dn>את</dn> the sovereign <dn>Your</dn> right-rulings, And <dn>Your</dn> righteousness to the Son of a sovereign. [2] Let <dn>Him</dn> rule <dn>את</dn> <dn>Your</dn> people with righteousness, And <dn>Your</dn> poor with right-ruling. [3] Let the mountains bring peace to the people, And the hills, by righteousness. [4] Let <dn>Him</dn> rightly rule <dn>את</dn> the poor of the people, Save <dn>את</dn> the children of the needy, And crush <dn>את</dn> the oppressor. [5] Let them fear <dn>You</dn> with the sun, shining And before the moon, in all generations. [6] Let <dn>Him</dn> come down like rain upon the mown grass, Like showers, watering the earth. [7] Let the righteous flourish in <dn>His</dn> days, With plenty of peace, Till the moon is no more. [8] And let <dn>Him</dn> rule from sea to sea, And from the River to the ends of the earth. [9] Let those dwelling in the desert bow before <dn>Him</dn>, And <dn>His</dn> enemies lick the dust. [10] Let the sovereigns of Tarshish and of the isles bring presents; The sovereigns of Sheḇa and Seḇa offer gifts. [11] And let all sovereigns bow down before <dn>Him</dn>, All nations serve <dn>Him</dn>. [12] For <dn>He</dn> delivers <dn>את</dn> the needy when he cries, And <dn>את</dn> the poor, who has no helper. [13] <dn>He</dn> spares the poor and needy, And <dn>He</dn> saves <dn>את</dn> the lives of the needy. [14] <dn>He</dn> redeems <dn>את</dn> their life from oppression and from violence; And their blood is precious in <dn>His</dn> eyes. [15] And <dn>He</dn> shall live, And the gold of Sheḇa be given to <dn>Him</dn>, And prayer be made for <dn>Him</dn> continually; Let <dn>Him</dn> be blessed all day long. [16] Let there be plenty of grain in the earth, On the top of the mountains, Let its fruit wave like Leḇanon, And those of the city flourish like grass of the earth. [17] Let <dn>His</dn> Name be forever, <dn>His</dn> Name continue before the sun; And let them bless themselves in <dn>Him</dn>; Let all nations call <dn>Him</dn> blessed. [18] Blessed be <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn>, <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl, <dn>He</dn> alone is doing wonders! [19] And blessed be <dn>His</dn> esteemed Name forever! And let all the earth Be filled with <dn>His</dn> esteem. Aměn and Aměn. [20] The prayers of Daviḏ the son of Yishai are ended.

readings.title: Unless the LORD Builds the House
readings.subtitle: The vanity of labor without God's blessing and the gift of children.
readings.text: [Psalm 127:1] If <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> does not build <dn>את</dn> the house, Its builders have laboured in vain. If <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> does not guard <dn>את</dn> the city, The watchman has stayed awake in vain. [2] In vain do you rise up early, To sit up late, to eat <dn>את</dn> the bread of toil; So <dn>He</dn> gives <dn>His</dn> beloved sleep. [3] Look, children are an inheritance from <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, The fruit of the womb is the reward. [4] As arrows in the hand of a mighty man, So are the children of one’s youth. [5] Blessed is the man Who has filled <dn>את</dn> his quiver with them. They are not ashamed, When they speak with their enemies in the gate.
